issue.title: flake-baseline gate never clears a renamed or deleted test's node ID
issue.description: tools/selection_health --fail-on-new-flake (reproducible_flake_nodeids, tests/_test_selection_health.py:183) flags a node ID as a reproducible flake whenever it fails across two disjoint change sets with no independent interleaved pass. When a flaky test is renamed or deleted, its old node ID can never appear in a passing run again -- there is no test left to run under that ID -- so it stays flagged as a reproducible flake forever, regardless of commit ordering, until someone manually bumps the baseline's effective-after cutoff past every one of its historical failures. This defect was masked by the cutoff bump landed for tests/reproducible_flake_baseline.txt as part of the sase-ct retirement (commit 83bb8a6f7), which incidentally cleared the concrete instance below, but the underlying mechanism gap remains and will silently recur the next time a flaky test is renamed. Concrete instance: tests/test_run_pytest_main.py::test_main_cost_mode_arms_only_the_cost_recorder was renamed to test_main_cost_mode_arms_cost_and_health_recorders by commit 1417de7db; the old node ID had a 14:33Z failure recorded against it and could never pass again under that name. Fix direction: the gate should skip (or report separately as stale, rather than as a live reproducible flake) any recorded node ID that is not present in the currently collected test suite. Lesser context to include, not separate scope: of 201 distinct record heads in the store at authoring time, git_commit_order_oracle failed to resolve exactly 1 (a commit from another workspace not present in that checkout); unresolved heads fall back to sequence order and sort last (_ordered_flake_candidate_runs, tests/_test_selection_health.py:244). At 1 of 201 this was not distorting the verdict, but it is the mechanism by which cross-workspace records could be mis-ordered -- worth a look if this ever becomes a larger fraction.
